summary.name: Bug tracking system
summary.one_liner: A Wikipedia article describing bug tracking systems (bugtrackers), software that records and manages reported software defects through their life cycle during development.
use_cases: tracking reported software bugs during development
managing product backlog and feature requests
letting end users submit bug reports
coordinating support teams with developers on issues
integrating bug tracking with version control
summary.what_it_does: The page explains what a bug tracking system is: a database-backed application that records facts about known bugs, such as report time, severity, reproduction steps, reporter, and assigned programmers. It describes the bug life cycle managed through status values, with configurable permissions and optional email notifications on changes. It covers how these systems give a centralized view of bugs and feature requests, feed product roadmaps, and are often part of integrated project management suites. It also mentions distributed bug trackers that work offline with distributed version control, naming Fossil, Veracity, FogBugz with Kiln, and ikiwiki.
notable: Distributed bug trackers that allow reading and updating reports while offline
Local bug tracker (LBT) for help desk teams, separate from the developer queue
Status-based life cycle with administrator-configurable statuses and permissions
caveats: Page is a general encyclopedia overview, not a specific product; no single tool is described
Reports on developer productivity from bug counts may be inaccurate because severity and complexity differ
